cross_references.note: Rosenthal FDCA (Civ §§1788-1788.33) covers original creditors excluded from federal FDCPA. Every collection case in California should plead both: FDCPA against third-party collectors + Rosenthal against all collectors. Rosenthal also allows punitive damages (§1788.30(b)) that federal FDCPA does not.

FDCPA + FCRA compound claim: debt collector reports disputed debt to CRA while §1692g dispute is pending = §1692e(8) FDCPA (communicating false credit info) + §1681s-2(b) FCRA (furnisher failed to correct after dispute). Dual statutory damages available.

If debt collection activity is part of a broader wire fraud scheme (collecting fraudulent debts via wire communications), FDCPA violations compound with §1343 wire fraud predicates. Collection of a debt known to be fraudulent via wire communications = both FDCPA §1692e(2)(A) and §1343 wire fraud.

Primary evidentiary source for FDCPA claims. Review all collection correspondence for: mini-Miranda disclosure (§1692e(11)), validation notice within 5 days (§1692g), whether disputes were sent and collection continued (§1692g), whether communications included false statements of debt status (§1692e(2)).
